focus: Emphatic possessive δικός agrees in gender/case with its noun – cite the card's actual form τους δικούς της χορούς, and drop the em dash.
The bare noun αγκαλιά (embrace) works as an adverb – 'we danced embrace-style'; keep that structural point, fix the em dash.
The past form καθυστέρησε marks one finished event (vs the ongoing past) – say it in plain words without the 'aorist' label.
English 'got lost' is just the passive form χάθηκε – Greek needs no extra 'got' word; frame the contrast, not the morphology label.
λόγω governs the genitive = 'because of' – real case-government insight, but the quoted example λόγω της κακοκαιρίας needs romanization.
αν γίνεται is the standard polite softener, lit. 'if it happens/becomes' – lead with the literal logic instead of re-glossing.
'Than' before a whole clause is απ' ό,τι, not plain από – keep that trap; romanize the quoted example.
The impression 'made itself to me' – μου έκανε εντύπωση flips the subject, same family as μου λείπει; the tip only glosses.
Doubling the adverb (σιγά σιγά = 'slowly slowly') is how Greek says little by little – reusable reduplication pattern, not just a gloss.
Lit. 'I make company with' – κάνω παρέα's literal logic is the hook the gloss omits.
Noun-of-noun uses the bare genitive φίλων, not από as English speakers expect – keep the contrast, fix the em dash.
μέσω + genitive = via/through – valid case-government point; the quoted run μέσω βίντεο needs romanization.
μπερδεύομαι με is the natural 'get confused by' – keep the anti-calque warning, remove the em dash.
μόλις means both 'as soon as' and 'just/barely' – context decides; the current tip gives only one meaning and leaves the example unromanized.
Same λόγω + genitive telling as el-3062 with only the noun swapped – one telling per angle; el-3062 carries it.
Days are μικρή/μεγάλη (small/big), never κοντή – genuine collocation trap; fix the em dash.
καιρός means both 'time' and 'weather' – με τον καιρό uses the time sense; that landmine is the earned hook.
όσο + past = 'as (time) went on' – keep the construction; romanize the quoted clause.
Greek 'takes' a decision (παίρνω απόφαση) where English makes one – the verb mismatch is the hook the gloss buries.
με τίποτα lit. 'with nothing' = 'not for anything / no way' – lead with the literal logic.
παρά = 'than' after a comparative (vs από) – keep; romanize the quoted example.
θα + past tense = 'would' – Greek's conditional in one move; romanize θα το ξανάκανα.
πως and ότι are interchangeable 'that' after belief verbs – keep; romanize both words.
κάθετα lit. 'vertically' – Greek disagrees vertically where English disagrees flatly; the literal hook is missing from the gloss.
στα + neuter plural adjective makes adverbs (στα σοβαρά 'for real', στα κρυφά 'secretly') – reusable pattern, not just a phrase gloss.
ας + verb = 'let's' – the real machinery of the phrase; teach the particle, not the whole-phrase gloss.
Dummy τα in τα βρίσκω ('find them') = come to terms – keep the idiom logic; romanize the second cited form τα βρήκαν.
Greek says 'white-black' (άσπρο μαύρο) – the reverse of English 'black and white'; that order flip is the earned fact.
εν + dative is a fossil of ancient Greek that survives only in set phrases like εν πάση περιπτώσει – that fact is the hook, 'fixed phrase' is not.
πολυλογώ lit. 'to many-word' – πολυ- compounds straight into verbs; give the literal logic instead of the bare gloss.
Question word + και να = '-ever' (όπως και να = however) – teach the reusable pattern; this card is the slice's one telling of it.
-οντας ending = English '-ing' (συνοψίζοντας 'summing up') – a reusable converb pattern hidden behind a phrase gloss.
Lit. 'at the bottom bottom' – doubled κάτω is Greek's 'at the end of the day'; the literal image is the earned hook.
τόσο…όσο = 'as…as' correlative – keep the mapping; romanize the quoted example τόσο απλό όσο.
Conclusions are 'taken out' in Greek (βγάζω συμπέρασμα), not drawn – the verb mismatch is the hook.
καλο- glued onto a verb = 'properly/well' (καλοσκεφτείς = think it over) – reusable prefix pattern, not a phrase gloss.
Anti-calque warning: native Greek says εν τέλει / στο κάτω κάτω, not the English calque στο τέλος της ημέρας – keep it, fix the em dash and romanize the calque.
ούτε…ούτε stacks onto δεν – Greek requires the double negative English forbids; romanize the quoted phrase.
